profile.purpose: Bind RFdiffusion3 as a second backbone arm beside RFdiffusion, each with its own ProteinMPNN sequence designer. small-run.template.json reaches the same module by replacing the RFdiffusion command, which leaves one arm running under another arm's name. This profile gives RFdiffusion3 its own adapter id, stage, and designer, so both arms can run in one campaign and be told apart in the candidate manifest.

The first applies the provider's published per-unit rates, USD 0.00125 per H100 second and USD 0.00007 per machine second, to 288.865 measured runner seconds. This rate divides that dearer figure by the 20 usable designs, so a ceiling refuses rather than under-quotes. No settled fal invoice line was captured for that run.
One settled Modal CPU run produced 2 validated 80-residue sequences for USD 0.00099581 in 3.102723 seconds. This rate divides that amount by 2, so it spreads container startup across both sequences.

stage_overrides.description: Design fixed-backbone SolubleCaliby v1 sequences for the RFdiffusion backbone arm. Ensemble conditioning is a separate adapter subcommand and is not selected by this profile.
Design ProteinMPNN sequences for the RFdiffusion3 backbone arm.

Generate the PXDesign arm on a fal deployment. The application returns its engine-native mmCIF and a chain-relabelled PDB bridge. It caps one request at 4 designs, so the adapter dispatches this phase as whole requests and records which one produced each row.
Design ProteinMPNN sequences for the PXDesign arm. The recorded PXDesign output carries placeholder residue names on the binder chain, so a sequence designer assigns residues downstream.

Generate the Proteina-Complexa arm on a fal deployment. The application co-designs a complex and its binder sequence, so no sequence-designer stage follows it. It serves one normalized chain A numbered from one and a fixed 64-residue binder, and it caps one request at 4 designs, so the adapter dispatches this phase as whole requests.
Generate BoltzGen complexes and binder sequences through the declared fal application; retain the native structures and metric evidence.

Design the FreeBindCraft arm end to end on a fal deployment: AlphaFold 2 multimer hallucination, the tool's own ProteinMPNN redesign, and re-prediction, with PyRosetta bypassed behind --no-pyrosetta. The stage publishes a staging set rather than the tool's accepted subset, because four of the tool's default filter thresholds compare a constant on that path, so every row carries the tool's verdict and this lane's screen ranks all of them. The application caps one request at 32 designs, so the adapter dispatches this phase as whole requests. No sequence-design stage follows, because the generator designs the sequence.
